How did a Ferrari pit crew make a children's hospital safer?
Great Ormond Street, London.
A baby has just survived heart surgery.
But one of the riskiest moments is still ahead.
The move from the operating theatre to intensive care.
Breathing tube, drips, monitors, all unplugged, moved, plugged back in.
Several teams, one tiny patient. Details get lost.
Then two of its doctors studied a Ferrari pit stop.
Twenty mechanics. One car. Done in seconds.
Nobody in anyone's way. Everyone with one job.
So they asked Ferrari for help.
Ferrari studied videos of the hospital's handovers.
The fix came straight from the pits.
One leader, like the lollipop man, runs everything.
Everyone gets one task, in a fixed order.
A checklist, so nothing is forgotten.
Technical errors fell by forty-two percent.
Missing information, almost cut in half.
A sport chasing tenths of a second taught doctors to protect what matters most.
So next time someone asks...
